{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}

'''Mercedes Maroto-Valer''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FREng}} is an engineer who holds the [[Robert Buchan]] Chair in Sustainable Energy Engineering at [[Heriot-Watt University]]. She is also director of the [[Research Centre for Carbon Solutions]] (RCCS)  at Heriot-Watt University. Maroto-Valer was awarded the [[Philip Leverhulme Prize]] for Engineering in 2009. She is a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]], the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]], the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] and the [[Institution of Chemical Engineers]]. 

== Life ==
Mercedes Maroto-Valer is an engineer working in Scotland. She earned her PhD at the [[University of Strathclyde]] in 1997, and conducted postdoctoral research at the [[University of Kentucky]] and [[Pennsylvania State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-02-24 |title=M. Mercedes Maroto-Valer |url=https://www.aiche.org/community/bio/m-mercedes-maroto-valer |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=www.aiche.org |language=en}}</ref> She was appointed as a reader at the University of Nottingham in 2005.<ref name=":1" /> She joined Heriot-Watt University in 2012.<ref name=":1" /> Maroto-Valer is Champion and Director of the UK Industrial Decarbonisation Research and Innovation Centre (IDRIC). Maroto-Valer is Deputy Principal (Global Sustainability) at [[Heriot-Watt University]]. She is also director of the Research Centre for Carbon Solutions (RCCS) at [[Heriot-Watt University]], where she holds the [[Robert Buchan]] Chair in Sustainable Energy Engineering.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-09-05 |title=Prestigious appointment to new Sustainable Energy Chair |url=https://www.hw.ac.uk/news/articles/2012/prestigious-appointment-to-new-sustainable.htm |access-date=2019-06-05 |website=Heriot-Watt University |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Who We Are - Research Centre for Carbon Solutions |url=https://rccs.hw.ac.uk/about-us/who-we-are.html |access-date=2019-06-05 |website=rccs.hw.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mercedes Maroto-Valer - Heriot-Watt University |url=https://www.hw.ac.uk/uk/about/profile/governance/mercedes-maroto-valer.htm |access-date=2021-01-26 |website=www.hw.ac.uk}}</ref> RCCS is a multidisciplinary centre delivering innovation for the wider deployment of low-carbon energy systems required for meeting net-zero targets. Maroto-Valer's research covers energy systems, CCUS [[carbon capture and storage|carbon dioxide capture and storage]], integration of hydrogen technologies and low carbon fuels.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2017-05-19 |title=Professor Mercedes Maroto-Valer FRSE |url=https://rse.org.uk/fellowship/fellow/professor-mercedes-maroto-valer-12704/ |access-date=11 April 2025 |website=The Royal Society of Edinburgh |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Awards ==
Maroto-Valer was elected a Fellow Royal Society of Chemistry in 2008, a Fellow of the Institute of Chemical Engineers in 2013, and a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 2015.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=IChemE |title=IChemE Fellow appointed as champion to help address industrial decarbonisation challenges |url=https://www.thechemicalengineer.com/news/icheme-fellow-appointed-as-champion-to-help-address-industrial-decarbonisation-challenges/ |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=www.thechemicalengineer.com}}</ref> She featured in the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]]'s 2019 ''Women in Science in Scotland'' exhibition, which celebrated some of Scotland’s leading female scientists.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Women in Science in Scotland: Professor Mercedes Maroto-Valer |url=https://rse.org.uk/whats-on/exhibition/women-science-exhibition/professor-mercedes-maroto-valer/ |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=Royal Society of Edinburgh |language=en-GB}}</ref> She received the 2009 [[Philip Leverhulme Prize]] for Engineering. <ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Philip Leverhulme Prizes 2009 {{!}} The Leverhulme Trust |url=https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/philip-leverhulme-prizes-2009 |access-date=2019-06-05 |website=www.leverhulme.ac.uk}}</ref> In 2019 she was awarded an honorary doctorate by [[Delft University of Technology]].<ref name=":1" /> In 2026 she was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]]<ref name="RAEng26">{{cite web |title=Royal Academy of Engineering welcomes 75 new Fellows |url=https://raeng.org.uk/news/new-fellows-2026/ |access-date=24 September 2026}}</ref><ref name="NF26">{{cite web |title=New Fellows 2026 |url=https://raeng.org.uk/about-us/fellowship/new-fellows-2026/ |access-date=24 September 2026}}</ref>.
